s: A company built an application based on AWS Lambda deployed in an AWS CloudFormation stack. The last production release of the web application introduced an issue that resulted in an outage lasting several minutes. A solutions architect must adjust the deployment process to support a canary release. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Create an alias for every new deployed version of the Lambda function. Use the AWS CLI update alias command with the routing-config parameter to distribute the load.
Deploy the application into a new CloudFormation stack. Use an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy to distribute the load.
Create a version for every new deployed Lambda function. Use the AWS CLI update-function configuration command with the routing-config parameter to distribute the load.
Configure AWS CodeDeploy and use CodeDeployDefault.OneAtATime in the Deployment configuration to distribute the load.

w.y: Lambda supports canary releases natively with weighted aliases. You publish a new version and set the alias routing configuration (update-alias --routing-config) to send a small share of traffic to it. Then you increase the share or roll back instantly. Routing configuration is an alias feature, not a function-configuration or version setting.

o.A: Correct: alias routing-config weights traffic between two versions, which is a canary release.
o.B: A second stack behind Route 53 weighted records is slow to shift because of DNS caching and doubles the infrastructure. It isn't Lambda's native canary mechanism.
o.C: update-function-configuration has no routing-config parameter, because weighted routing only exists on aliases.
o.D: CodeDeployDefault.OneAtATime is an EC2/on-premises configuration. For Lambda you would use a Canary or Linear configuration.

s: Implement Lambda canary deployments using a weighted alias
Implementing Canary Deployments of AWS Lambda Functions with Alias Traffic Shifting
